title: Data Collection Without Proper Consent
description: Wearable device collects sensitive sensor data (GPS traces, exercise sessions, device ID) without verified user consent or legal basis for processing.

title: User Identification Through Device ID
description: Device ID transmitted to companion app enables persistent user identification and cross-device tracking across sessions.

title: Excessive Data Retention
description: Sensor data batches (GPS traces, timestamps) may be retained longer than necessary for the stated purpose, increasing privacy risk.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure During Sync
description: Sensitive data (GPS traces, device ID) transmitted from wearable to companion app may be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties during sync.

title: Data Used Beyond Original Purpose
description: Collected sensor data may be used for purposes beyond exercise tracking (e.g., marketing, third-party sharing) without user knowledge.

title: Insufficient User Notification
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what data is collected, how it's used, or who it's shared with before device sync occurs.

title: Insufficient notification of data collection
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what personal health data (calories, meals, weight) is being collected, how it will be used, and with whom it may be shared.

title: Unintended data collection
description: The companion app may collect additional health-related or personal data beyond the explicitly logged entries (e.g., location, device identifiers, usage patterns) without user awareness or consent.

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: The app may not fully comply with privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) regarding the collection, processing, and storage of special category health data, potentially leading to legal and reputational risks.

title: Inappropriate information use
description: The collected health data may be used for purposes beyond the stated purpose of tracking calorie intake, meals, and weight, such as targeted advertising or selling to third parties.

title: Unintended Disclosure During Transmission
description: Health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) transmitted from the Companion Mobile App (P2) to the Health Log Store (DS1) could be intercepted or exposed during transmission, potentially exposing sensitive personal health information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network connection that may not be fully secured.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: The app may collect more health data than necessary for its intended purpose, including calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions, which could be more sensitive than required for basic fitness tracking.
assumptions: Assumes the app collects all three types of health data simultaneously.

title: Inaccurate Health Data
description: Health logs entered by users may contain inaccuracies in calorie intake, weight history, or exercise sessions, leading to incorrect health information being stored and potentially affecting user health decisions.
assumptions: Assumes users may input data incorrectly or the app may not validate data accuracy.

title: Insufficient Notice of Data Collection
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what health data is being collected, how it will be used, and who will have access to it before providing consent.
assumptions: Assumes the app's privacy policy may not be clear or accessible to all users.

title: Inadequate Data Destruction
description: Health logs stored in the Health Log Store (DS1) may not be securely deleted when users request deletion or when data retention periods expire, potentially leaving sensitive health information accessible.
assumptions: Assumes the data store may not implement proper secure deletion procedures.

title: Legal Basis for Data Processing
description: The collection and storage of health logs may lack a clear legal basis under applicable privacy regulations, particularly given the sensitive nature of health information.
assumptions: Assumes the app operates in a jurisdiction with strict privacy regulations like GDPR or HIPAA.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: The data handling practices for health logs may not comply with applicable privacy regulations and industry standards, potentially resulting in legal and reputational risks.
assumptions: Assumes the app may not have comprehensive compliance measures in place.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: GPS location traces stored in DS2 could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leaked, or shared without user consent, potentially leading to privacy violations and stalking risks.

title: Unintended Use of Location Data
description: Location history data could be used for purposes other than the intended navigation or tracking, such as targeted advertising, behavioral profiling, or third-party data sharing without explicit user consent.

title: Lack of User Control Over Location Data
description: Users may not have adequate controls to manage, delete, or export their location history once stored in DS2, limiting their ability to control their personal information.

title: Inaccuracy of Location Data
description: GPS data collected by the app may be inaccurate due to signal interference, leading to incorrect location records in DS2 that could mislead users or affect location-based services.

title: Unintended Destruction of Location Data
description: Location history data in DS2 could be deleted or destroyed without proper safeguards, potentially violating user expectations and privacy regulations regarding data retention and deletion requests.

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Data
description: Health Analytics Service may expose sensitive health data (calorie, weight, exercise logs) to unauthorized individuals or systems during processing or storage.

title: Data Leakage During Analytics Processing
description: Health data could be inadvertently disclosed during the analytics processing phase, potentially through logging, debugging, or system misconfiguration.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: The analytics service reads calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions which may exceed what is necessary for the specific health-condition analysis purpose.

title: Insufficient User Notification
description: Users may not be adequately informed about how their health data is being used for analytics across sessions, including the scope and purpose of data processing.

title: Data Quality Compromise
description: Health data quality may be compromised if the analytics service processes incomplete, inaccurate, or outdated health log data, affecting analysis reliability.

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk
description: Health data processing may not fully comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) regarding sensitive health information handling.

title: Processing without adequate legal basis
description: Location history may be processed for health analytics without sufficient legal basis or explicit consent from users.

title: Excessive location data collection
description: Location history across all sessions may be collected beyond what is strictly necessary for deriving daily routine and movement patterns.

title: Excessive data retention
description: Location history may be retained longer than necessary for health analytics purposes, increasing privacy risk.

title: Inaccurate location data
description: Health analytics derived from location history may be inaccurate due to GPS errors or data collection issues, affecting user trust.

title: Unintended access to location data
description: Location history may be accessed by unauthorized parties during analytics processing, potentially exposing sensitive movement patterns.

title: Lack of notification to users
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their location history is being used to derive health analytics and movement patterns.

title: Inaccurate or incomplete health insights
description: The analytics service may return inferred health insights that are inaccurate, incomplete, or based on outdated data, potentially leading to incorrect health decisions by users.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health information
description: Health condition risk indicators and routine summaries contain sensitive personal health information that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission to the companion app.

title: Insufficient user notification about data sharing
description: Users may not be adequately notified about what health insights are being shared, with whom, and for what purposes when analytics results are returned to the companion app.

title: Unintended use of health insights
description: The health insights returned to the companion app may be used for purposes other than what the user intended, such as insurance underwriting, employment decisions, or third-party data sharing.

title: Non-compliance with health data regulations
description: The transmission of health condition risk indicators and routine summaries may not comply with applicable health data regulations such as HIPAA, GDPR, or other privacy laws.

title: Inferred health indicators may lack legitimate basis
description: The app displays inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals to the user. There is a risk that these inferences may not have a legitimate basis or may be based on insufficient data, potentially causing unnecessary concern or medical decisions based on unreliable information.

title: Inferred health indicators may be inaccurate
description: The inferred condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) may not be accurate or complete, potentially leading to incorrect health assessments or unnecessary anxiety for the user.

title: Health data may be used beyond intended purpose
description: The health-related data displayed to the user may be used for purposes beyond the intended dashboard display, such as sharing with third parties or using for commercial purposes without explicit consent.

title: Potential non-compliance with health data regulations
description: The display of eating-disorder and diabetes risk indicators may not be fully compliant with health data protection regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR), particularly regarding informed consent and data handling practices.

title: Excessive data collection for analytics
description: Health Analytics Service may collect and transfer more health and location data than necessary for the analytics purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Data integrity risk during replication
description: Third-party cloud hosting provider may experience data corruption, loss, or unauthorized modification during data replication, compromising data integrity of health and location datasets.

title: Insufficient anonymization of health data
description: Health and location data stored at cloud provider may not be adequately anonymized or de-identified, creating re-identification risks for individuals.

title: Legal basis for data processing unclear
description: Health Analytics Service may not have clear legal basis or appropriate consent for transferring and storing sensitive health data at third-party cloud provider.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Third-party cloud hosting provider may not be fully compliant with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) regarding health data storage and replication.
